subject: Lightweight MAP: PoC activation checklist & wiring steps
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@medtechcorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medtechcorp.com
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lightweight MAP: PoC activation checklist & wiring steps

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We want to move forward with a short, 2-week PoC focused on inference latency and cost profiles for our batch workloads. To keep things light, could you send over a mutual action plan that covers the minimal environment setup we need on our side? Specifically we need clarity on:

- Org setup and user roles (who should be invited on Redwood)
- Temporary API keys vs long-lived keys for the evaluation
- IP allowlist ranges for the test endpoints (we manage our egress rules)
- Whether VPC peering is required for the initial phase or can be deferred
- Expected owners and approximate dates for each step

If you can draft a compact checklist (one page) with owners and a proposed timeline, that would help us unblock procurement and scheduling.

Prefer kickoff early next week.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Carter
Head of Platform, MedTech Corp
sam.carter@medtechcorp.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@medtechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lightweight MAP: PoC activation checklist & wiring steps

Sam —

Appreciate the clear list. I put together a lightweight MAP and attached a short checklist (medtech-map-draft-v2.pdf) plus a CSV template for the IP ranges we need (network-allowlist.csv). Below is the condensed plan — owners and target dates are in parentheses. We kept the timeline to two weeks as requested.

1) Kickoff call & environment sign-off — (Irene) — Target: Tue, 2028-09-03
   - Confirm PoC scope (batch workload sample sizes, latency targets)

2) Org invite & role assignment — (MedTech: Sam; Redwood: Priyom) — Target: Wed, 2028-09-04
   - Add two MedTech users (Platform lead + Dev lead) to Redwood eval org with Viewer/Tester roles

3) API keys provisioning — (Redwood: Priyom) — Target: Thu, 2028-09-05
   - We will create short-lived evaluation API keys (7-day rotation) and provide a key rotation plan if you want longer duration

4) IP allowlist publication — (MedTech: Sam) — Target: Thu, 2028-09-05
   - Please populate the attached CSV with CIDR blocks; we will whitelist on our side once received

5) VPC peering (optional for initial run) — (Marissa) — Decision by Fri, 2028-09-06
   - Recommendation: start with hosted endpoints + allowlist to move faster; propose peering only if you need private connectivity or high throughput

6) Test execution & metrics collection — (MedTech + Redwood) — Window: 2028-09-06 to 2028-09-17
   - We’ll share a small test harness and a template for the metrics we’ll collect (latency p50/p95, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens)

7) Wrap + next steps — (Irene + Sam) — Target: 2028-09-18

Attachments: medtech-map-draft-v2.pdf (MAP checklist v0.2), network-allowlist.csv (CIDR template)

Let us know if procurement needs a separate copy of the MAP for sign-off. If that looks good, can we schedule the kickoff for Tue 9/3 at 10am PT?

Best,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Lightweight MAP: PoC activation checklist & wiring steps

Irene — thank you, that draft is helpful. A few questions before we finalize: 

- For the short-lived API keys, is there an automated rotation endpoint we can call, or will keys be issued manually each week?
- For the IP allowlist CSV: we have split egress between two subnets. Can we include both ranges?
- On peering: our security team may insist on peering once test data is in scope. If we approve peering later, is there a clean migration path from hosted endpoints to peering without re-issuing keys to the app?

Procurement asked if you can provide a one-page statement of work (SOW) with roles and expected deliverables for sign-off — we can attach the MAP to that.

Sam

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, procurement@medtechcorp.com
Date: Mon, 02 Sep 2028 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lightweight MAP: PoC activation checklist & wiring steps — answers & kickoff confirmation

Sam / team —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Short answers and confirmations below; expanded notes are in the attached MAP v0.2.

- API keys: We’ll provision short-lived keys programmatically. Priyom will create an enrollment token for your engineering lead; it can be used to request 7-day keys via our rotation API (we’ll share the endpoint and example curl). If you need a longer lived key for automation, we can set up a 30-day key with automatic rotation and webhook notifications. (Owner: Priyom)

- IP allowlist: Yes — include both subnets in the CSV. We will whitelist all provided CIDRs; please add a contact/phone for emergency updates. (Owner: Sam)

- Migration to peering: We support graceful migration — keys do not need to be reissued when switching to VPC peering. We configure routing and endpoint aliasing so your app can target the same hostname once peering is active. Peering will require a short maintenance window and a brief DNS/route swap. (Owner: Marissa)

- SOW for procurement: I’ll attach a one-page SOW template to the MAP and copy procurement on a DocuSign link for execution.

Kickoff: Tue, 2028-09-03 at 10:00 AM PT works for our team — I’ve tentatively added it to the invite. Please confirm.

Next immediate ask for MedTech: fill the attached network-allowlist.csv and reply-all so we can whitelist before the kickoff.

Best,
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
